Favaro Veneto (mainland district near Marco Polo Airport) — Venice, Italy

Relatively safer day Average night

In detail

Extensive searches of Il Gazzettino, La Nuova Venezia, VeneziaToday, La Piazza Web, and Antenna Tre/Medianordest turned up no pattern of muggings, tourist-targeted pickpocketing, or organized crime in Favaro Veneto, Campalto or Dese — unlike central Venice, which has well-documented tourist-theft problems. The most significant dated finding is a real, resolved 2026 case: starting after Easter, a 40-year-old Favaro resident carried out a months-long stalking and intimidation campaign against a relative, including death threats, a garage arson, and setting fire to a well-known local baker's car; press described the neighbourhood as feeling under siege until his arrest in August 2026. Older, dated items (2019-2022) show isolated but real incidents — a drug-dealing operation broken up at a hotel, a knife altercation in the pedestrian square, an armed-robbery suspect arrested hiding in a Favaro apartment, and a violent multi-vehicle chase with reported gunshots near Campalto's Via Orlanda in December 2022 — but nothing recurring or current enough to indicate an ongoing hotspot. Regional data shows Veneto ranks second nationally for home burglaries in 2024, a province-wide trend rather than a Favaro-specific one. Overall this is a quiet, largely residential and airport-adjacent district with no daytime safety concerns found; night is marked yellow reflecting the genuine, recent (2026) arson/stalking episode and the region's elevated home-burglary backdrop, not any pattern of street crime against residents or visitors. Sources checked: Antenna Tre / Medianordest (antennatre.medianordest.it); VeneziaToday (veneziatoday.it); Il Gazzettino (ilgazzettino.it); La Piazza Web (lapiazzaweb.it); La Nuova Venezia (nuovavenezia.it); Comune di Venezia - Live (live.comune.venezia.it); Il Nuovo Terraglio (ilnuovoterraglio.it).
